checks.claim: Air suspension systems use a compressor to fill an air tank, which then fills the air springs through valves.
checks.why: AccuAir and HowStuffWorks: the compressor fills the tank slowly, the tank's stored air fills the bags quickly through the valve block's fill and dump valves.

sources.title: How Does Air Suspension Work? - AccuAir
How Air Suspension Systems Work - HowStuffWorks

checks.claim: Compressed air holds moisture that condenses as water in the air tank, so air ride systems use water traps or drains.
checks.why: Bag Riders and AccuAir: water collects in the tank and lines; water traps and tank drains remove it.

sources.title: What Are Water Traps, And Why Do I Need Them? - Bag Riders
How To Drain An Air Suspension Tank - AccuAir

checks.claim: Many air suspension systems use height sensors at each corner and can lower the car automatically at highway speed.
checks.why: Audi, Mercedes and Tesla manuals describe automatic lowering at speed; supplier pages list height sensors as standard components.

sources.title: Audi Q7 2015 manual: air suspension lowering at speed
Tesla Model X manual: Air Suspension

checks.claim: Air suspension still needs shock absorbers to stop the car from bouncing.
checks.why: Air springs cushion but give little damping; hydraulic shock absorbers provide it, or the car bounces at its natural frequency.

sources.title: Air Suspension and Replacement Dampers - Balance Motorsport
